facts.statement: Brillanceausuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms.
The genus Brillanceausuchus was described by Michard, de Broin, Brunet, and Hell in 1990.
Brillanceausuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
Fossils of Brillanceausuchus date from the Valanginian to Barremian stages, between 137.05 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Valanginian to Barremian (137.05 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of the genus Brillanceausuchus.
Fossils of Brillanceausuchus have been discovered in Early Cretaceous rocks in Cameroon.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in Early Cretaceous–age rocks of Cameroon.

facts.statement: In Brillanceausuchus, parts of the pterygoid bones form the front edge of the secondary choana, separating it from the palatine bones.
facts.quote: Parts of the pterygoid bones make up the rostral margin of the choana and thus separate it from the palatines

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the position of the secondary choana is a homoplastic trait, meaning it evolved independently in Brillanceausuchus and Eusuchia rather than being inherited from a common ancestor.
facts.quote: This characteristic was once thought to be characteristic of Eusuchia, but its presence in Brillanceausuchus suggests that the trait is homoplasic

facts.statement: Brillanceausuchus is classified as a member of the extinct family Paralligatoridae.
facts.quote: Brillanceausuchus is an extinct genus of paralligatorid crocodyliforms.

facts.statement: The parent group of Brillanceausuchus is the family Paralligatoridae.
Brillanceausuchus belongs to the class Reptilia.
The type species of the genus Brillanceausuchus is Brillanceausuchus babouriensis.

rejected.statement: Brillanceausuchus is notable for the unique position of the secondary choana within its palate.
rejected.quote: The genus is notable for the position of the secondary choana within its palate.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'position of the secondary choana within its palate'
